process_area.title: Cooperative & Social Enterprise Sourcing Strategy & Onboarding

fields.Participants: Sustainability Sourcing Mgr, Category Mgmt (links to VS-01), Sustainability Lead (links to VS-25), Legal, Finance
fields.Trigger: Annual category strategy; ESG/social-impact target setting (links to VS-25); new community-partnership opportunity

workflows.name: Cooperative Sourcing Strategy & Category Coverage Planning

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "enterprises are competitive and impactful" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-post of "posture, and impact KPIs" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approves strategy and budget" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-511 (ensure controlled execution — Cooperative & Social Enterprise Sourcing Strategy & Onboarding (PA-94.1).)
- operational: traceable impact KPIs and third-party certification (W3130)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Greenwashing risk**: Coop-sourcing claims without substance damage brand; mitigated by traceable impact KPIs and third-party certification (W3130)
System Touchpoints: - Assortment/sourcing master (links to VS-01/VS-03); ESG scorecard (links to VS-25); budget (links to VS-33)

steps.activity: Sustainability Sourcing Manager + Category (links to VS-01) scan assortment for categories where coops/social-enterprises are competitive and impactful: garden/plants, home décor/furniture, handcrafted hardware, baskets/packaging, indigenous materials; size addressable spend and impact

Set category-by-category coop-sourcing targets (% of category buy), fair-trade posture, and impact KPIs (livelihoods supported, beneficiaries, fair-wage premium); align to ESG roadmap (links to VS-25)
Steering committee approves strategy and budget (capacity-building fund, advance-financing facility); publish to Category plans and integrate to S&OP demand signal (links to VS-02)

fields.Participants: Sustainability Sourcing Mgr, CDA-accredited Coop Dev't Specialist, Quality, Legal, Finance, Sustainability Lead
fields.Trigger: Strategy defines a category gap; coop fair/trade mission; government livelihood program referral

workflows.name: Cooperative & Social Enterprise Identification & Due Diligence

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "enterprise incubators, indigenous peoples' councils" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "record distinct from VS-03 mainstream" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "validate product fit" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-511 (ensure controlled execution — Cooperative & Social Enterprise Sourcing Strategy & Onboarding (PA-94.1).)
- operational: on-site visit, member rosters, and CDA/NCIP verification
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-representation risk**: Coop overstates capacity/impact; mitigated by on-site visit, member rosters, and CDA/NCIP verification
System Touchpoints: - Vendor master with coop/social-enterprise flag (links to VS-29); supplier risk (links to VS-68); quality sample (links to VS-31)

steps.activity: Sources of candidates: CDA registry, DTI-BMED, DSWD-SLP/DOLE livelihood graduates, WFTO/local fair-trade rosters, social-enterprise incubators, indigenous peoples' councils (NCIP), trade missions; referral from VS-25 partners

Sustainability Sourcing Mgr performs due diligence: legal status (CDA coop registration / SEC social-enterprise / DTI business name), governance, financial viability, production capacity, labor standards (no child/forced labor — links to VS-86), environmental practices, references; documents as vendor master record distinct from VS-03 mainstream

Quality/Sustainability validate product fit: sample evaluation, raw-material provenance (links to VS-71 anti-counterfeit where relevant), compliance with product safety (links to VS-31/VS-89), and social impact baseline (members, wages, communities); recommend proceed/defer/decline

fields.Participants: Sustainability Sourcing Mgr, Quality, Capacity-Building Partner, Finance, IT, Coop Representatives

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "count, beneficiary community, governance, bank account for…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-capture of "Sustainability Sourcing Mgr plans certification path" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-68 (ensure cooperative vendor qualification & settlement integrity.)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Capability gap risk**: Coop cannot meet spec/quality at volume; mitigated by capacity-building (W3117) and pilot-first sourcing
System Touchpoints: - Vendor master with extended coop attributes (links to VS-29); certification register; quality (links to VS-31)

steps.activity: Sustainability Sourcing Mgr onboards coop into vendor master with extended attributes: coop name, CDA registration #, member count, beneficiary community, governance, bank account for direct-to-beneficiary settlement, certification status; integrates to VS-03 vendor portal if applicable

Quality/ Capacity-Building Partner conduct capability assessment against BuildRight product specification: production capacity (units/week), lead time, quality consistency, packaging/labeling ability, traceability, and gap list

Sustainability Sourcing Mgr plans certification path: target fair-trade/social-enterprise certifications (WFTO, local fair-trade, Go Lokal!, DTI-BMED), product-safety marks (PS/ICC, FDA-LTO where applicable — links to VS-22/VS-31); set timeline

fields.Participants: Sustainability Sourcing Mgr, Category (links to VS-01), Legal, Finance, Coop Representatives

workflows.name: Cooperative Pricing, Fair-Trade Terms & Contract Negotiation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "document fair-wage premium vs." (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-report of "reporting obligations, audit rights" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "record contract and pricing in master data" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-511 (ensure controlled execution — Cooperative & Social Enterprise Sourcing Strategy & Onboarding (PA-94.1).)
- operational: living-wage pricing methodology and documented premium
Pain Points / Risks: - **Price-asymmetry risk**: BuildRight imposing mainstream price discipline on coops undermines fair-trade; mitigated by living-wage pricing methodology and documented premium
System Touchpoints: - Contract repository (links to VS-22/VS-36); pricing master (links to VS-01/VS-29); AP direct-pay (links to VS-15)

steps.activity: Sustainability Sourcing Mgr/Category determine fair-trade price: cost-of-sustainable-production + living-wage labor cost + fair margin (not least-cost); benchmark vs. mainstream (links to VS-01) and fair-trade floors; document fair-wage premium vs. prevailing

Legal/Sustainability negotiate contract: price, volume commitment (minimum offtake to support coop planning), payment terms (favorable — e.g., 50% advance, balance on delivery), exclusivity/IP (indigenous designs — links to IPRA W3134), tenure, impact-reporting obligations, audit rights

Sustainability Sourcing Mgr/Finance set up direct-to-coop-account / direct-to-beneficiary settlement (links to W3126) and advance-financing facility (links to W3127); record contract and pricing in master data (links to VS-29)

fields.Participants: Sustainability Sourcing Mgr, Capacity-Building Partner, Quality, Coop Representatives, Government Partners
fields.Trigger: Capability gap; demand growth; livelihood-program grant

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-report of "Coop Representatives confirm capacity, accept production plan, and report" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-511 (ensure controlled execution — Cooperative & Social Enterprise Sourcing Strategy & Onboarding (PA-94.1).)
- operational: enterprise-graduation path (W3133) and multi-buyer diversification
Pain Points / Risks: - **Capacity-build dependency risk**: Coop becomes over-reliant on BuildRight programs; mitigated by enterprise-graduation path (W3133) and multi-buyer diversification
System Touchpoints: - Demand/production plan (links to VS-02); quality (links to VS-31); capacity-building tracker

steps.activity: Capacity-Building Partner (NGO, government livelihood officer, technical trainer) delivers targeted programs: production technique, quality/standardization, packaging/labeling, business/financial literacy, digital tools; co-funded by BuildRight capacity fund or government livelihood grant

Sustainability Sourcing Mgr aligns BuildRight demand plan (links to VS-02) to coop production capacity and harvest/seasonal cycle (W3123); plans production in batches that fit coop labor and lead time

Coop Representatives confirm capacity, accept production plan, and report progress; Quality provides feedback loop to continuously lift capability; graduate coops to larger commitments (links to W3133)

fields.Participants: Quality, Sustainability Sourcing Mgr, Coop Representatives
fields.Trigger: New coop onboarding; new SKU; quality drift

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "checklist, sampling plan" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-inspect of "inspection at BuildRight DC" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-68 (ensure cooperative vendor qualification & settlement integrity.)
- operational: training, AQL sampling, and design-for-manufacturability input
Pain Points / Risks: - **Variable-quality risk**: Handcrafted output varies; mitigated by training, AQL sampling, and design-for-manufacturability input
System Touchpoints: - Quality/spec master (links to VS-31); receiving inspection (links to VS-04); defect feedback

steps.activity: Quality defines product specification: dimensions, materials, finish, packaging/labeling, lot/traceability codes, product-safety compliance (links to VS-31/VS-89); translates to visual standard and acceptance criteria understandable to coop artisans
Quality delivers on-site training to coop: spec walkthrough, defect examples, self-inspection checklist, sampling plan (AQL); certifies coop's designated quality lead

Quality implements incoming inspection at BuildRight DC (links to VS-04 W3 inbound): AQL sampling, defect classification (critical/major/minor), disposition (accept/reject/rework), and feedback to coop for continuous improvement

fields.Participants: Sustainability Lead, Sustainability Sourcing Mgr, Government Agency Liaison, Coop Representatives, Legal
fields.Trigger: New community identified; government livelihood-program cycle (DSWD-SLP, DOLE livelihood, DTI-BMED, TESDA)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "Sustainability Lead structures co-funding/grant" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "reports livelihood outcomes to government partner and into BuildRight impact…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-511 (ensure controlled execution — Cooperative & Social Enterprise Sourcing Strategy & Onboarding (PA-94.1).)
- operational: agency-level (not personality-level) MOA and multi-partner diversification
Pain Points / Risks: - **Political-turnover risk**: LGU/agency leadership change disrupts partnership; mitigated by agency-level (not personality-level) MOA and multi-partner diversification
System Touchpoints: - Partnership/MOA register (links to VS-36); impact scorecard (links to VS-25); government reporting

steps.activity: Sustainability Lead/Agency Liaison engage government livelihood programs: DSWD-SLP (Sustainable Livelihood Program), DOLE livelihood, DTI-BMED (Bureau of MSME Development), TESDA skills training, NCIP for indigenous communities; align programs to BuildRight offtake needs

Sustainability Lead structures co-funding/grant: BuildRight provides offtake commitment + technical assist; government provides seed grant/ equipment/ training; coop commits to livelihood outcomes; Legal reviews MOA
Sustainability Lead reports livelihood outcomes to government partner and into BuildRight impact scorecard (links to W3129); sustains partnership across program cycles

fields.Participants: Sustainability Sourcing Mgr, Category, Finance, Legal, Quality, Coop Representatives
fields.Trigger: Coop non-performance; capacity exhaustion; category exit; coop graduates to mainstream vendor

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "documents exit rationale" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-identify of "identify replacement source" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "record impact outcomes for posterity" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-511 (ensure controlled execution — Cooperative & Social Enterprise Sourcing Strategy & Onboarding (PA-94.1).)
- operational: responsible-exit policy gate — cure-period log, transition-support plan, and exit sign-off before any termination
Pain Points / Risks: - **Harmful-exit risk**: Sudden termination harms dependent community; mitigated by cure period, transition support, and responsible-exit policy
System Touchpoints: - Contract/termination (links to VS-22); final settlement (links to VS-15); impact record

steps.activity: Sustainability Sourcing Mgr documents exit rationale (performance, capacity, strategic); for under-performance, provides cure period and improvement plan before termination (fair-trade duty of care)

Category/Planning identify replacement source (another coop, mainstream vendor — links to VS-03, or private label — links to VS-41); transition inventory and PO commitments without stranding coop (honour open POs)

Legal terminates contract per terms; Finance settles final dues; Sustainability Lead supports transition (graduation to mainstream, alternative buyers, or wind-down with dignity); record impact outcomes for posterity
